title: Maximum Number of Operations With the Same Score II
summary: Given an array of integers, you can perform operations by deleting either the first two elements, the last two elements, or the first and last elements.
statement: Given an array of integers, you can perform operations by deleting either the first two elements, the last two elements, or the first and last elements. Each operation's score is the sum of the deleted elements. Find the maximum number of operations that can be performed such that all operations have the same score.
constraints: nums contains at least two positive integers.
Each operation deletes the first pair, last pair, or two endpoints; every chosen pair must have the same sum as the first operation.
Return the maximum possible number of deletions.
hints: Only three first-operation scores are possible; after fixing one, the remaining state is an interval.
Memoize the best continuation for each [left,right] interval under each candidate score.
Try matching first-two, endpoints, and last-two transitions; evaluate all three initial removals and add the first operation.
Every legal deletion maps to exactly one interval transition, and memoization explores all choices without recomputing overlapping intervals.
editorial: Every legal deletion maps to exactly one interval transition, and memoization explores all choices without recomputing overlapping intervals.

tests.explanation: Choose score five: remove the first pair, then both endpoints twice, for three operations.
With score five, removing the first pair then the last pair yields two operations, which is optimal.
